plain_text:
11/12/2026 - Minutes
Call to Order
Members Present: Mike O’Brien, Chair; Brian Colombini; Ruby Tetrick; Matt Gile; James 
Paradissis
City Staff Present: Ravi Venkataraman, Director of City Planning; Jon Rauscher, Director of 
Public Works; Ryan Lambert, City Engineer
Guests Present: Thomas Renner, Mayor; Michael Miller; Eli Ogilvie
Call to Order by: Mike
Meeting Start Time: 6:31 pm
Minutes Recorded by: Ravi
Changes to the Agenda
None
Public Comment
None
Approve Previous Meeting Minutes
Motion by: Brian
Second: Ruby
Decision: 4-0 (Ruby abstained)
Discussion: Winooski Comprehensive Plan – Municipal Infrastructure section
Ravi gave an overview of the meeting materials, and specified that the focus of the discussion 
tonight is on transportation. Ravi said that he needs to draft content on water, sewer, 
stormwater, public transit, and energy, and that he has the information to draft the content.
Mike asked if the City currently has an Enhanced Energy Plan. Ravi said that the 2019 Master 
Plan does, that Chittenden County Regional Planning Commission (CCRPC) has provided him 
all the needed data to complete the Enhanced Energy Plan, and that he needs to draft the plan 
in accordance to the statutory requirements.
Ravi presented the draft transportation planning map. Ravi pointed out Malletts Bay Avenue and 
the public’s desire for improvements on the corridor. Mike asked about the feasibility of 
improvements within the right-of-way. Jon said that Malletts Bay Avenue is identified in the City’s 
Walk Bike Plan, and that a public process is needed to determine priorities to include and not 
include within the narrow right-of-way. Jon said that a similar process for East Allen Street took 
a year. Ravi said that for Malletts Bay Avenue, the process could be longer than a year because 
the transportation and land use elements need to be investigated. Mike asked if the planning 
would go through CCRPC. Jon affirmed. Jon said that if Colchester were to partner with the City 
on the planning study, the planning study could come at no cost to both municipalities Jon said 
that there are financial constraints to consider, as the City has taken on debt from recent 
projects and from upcoming projects, and that he doesn’t see large reconstruction projects 
happening within the next eight years. Mike asked about Colchester’s plans for future 
connections to Malletts Bay Avenue. Jon pointed out the lack of bike and pedestrian 
infrastructure on the Colchester side of Malletts Bay Avenue. Ravi pointed out the presence of 
wetlands on the Colchester side of Malletts Bay Avenue. Brian highlighted the need for 
pedestrian safety for crossings on Malletts Bay Avenue. James discussed the utility of having 
bike infrastructure on Malletts Bay Avenue. Mike asked about traffic counts on Malletts Bay 
Avenue. Jon estimated that the traffic counts are about a third of the traffic on Main Street. Ryan 
said that traffic on Malletts Bay Avenue is expected to increase during bridge construction, and 
that any study should take place after bridge construction when the traffic returns to normal 
rates. Ravi said that the transportation planning map is a long-term visioning document, and that 
for any planning study to occur, planning and public works will need the capacity and to work 
together to complete a thorough study. Brian said that he would like to see the Malletts Bay 
Avenue and West Spring Street intersection improved. Jon said that the intersection will not be 
an easy fix, and may need curbing, money and personnel to carry out the project.
Mike asked about Weaver Street. Ravi said that Weaver Street has had some history with bike 
infrastructure, and that a study is needed to think deeper about bicycle and pedestrian 
improvements along the corridor.
Mike asked about East Spring Street. Jon and Ravi reviewed the forthcoming improvements to 
East Spring Street as part of the Hoods Crossing signal improvements. Jon said that the City 
may look into expanding the sidewalk along East Spring Street past Russell Street, and that 
East Spring Street, North Street and Dion Street are identified priority sidewalk projects. Mike 
asked why the sidewalk on East Spring Street will be placed on the south side. Ryan explained 
that the location of subsurface infrastructure, the potential impacts of turning movements at the 
intersection on pedestrian safety, and costs.
Mike asked about West Spring Street. Ravi said that the intent is to be determined, and that the 
City would need to consider how it is coordinating bicycle and pedestrian improvements on 
Malletts Bay and East Spring Street to ensure wider connectivity. Ryan added that the pavement 
condition of Spring Street is poor, and that resurfacing is likely to happen before any 
investigations into improving connectivity.
Ravi said that North Street is in need of a sidewalk north of Pine Street because the 
neighborhood is cut off from the rest of the City. Mike asked about the presence of sidewalks in 
the northern portion of North Street. Jon said that the side streets off North Street—Cedar 
Street, Dufresne Drive, and Brisson Court—have sidewalks but North Street does not. Matt 
underscored the challenges of walking students from the school to Landry Park safely, and the 
options are limited. Jon reviewed the citywide traffic calming review, stating that North Street 
qualified for traffic calming, which may lend to building out a sidewalk in the long term. Mike 
asked about the access between North Street and Tigan Street. Ryan said that the City owns 
the parcel on which a path exists, but no formal right-of-way from Tigan Street to the beginning 
of that path. Jon said hat he has encouraged community members to reach out to the 
businesses on Tigan Street to formalize the connection between Tigan Street and the path to 
North Street.
Ravi said that the City has completed a scoping study for Lafountain Street and Dion Street, and 
that the City will need to work on the next steps towards implementation. Jon said that Public 
Works looks to coordinate utility improvements with roadway improvements, that the water main 
on Lafountain Street has had many water breaks, and that replacing the water main is 
highlighted in the City’s water distribution master plan. Jon said that the sidewalk on Dion Street 
is needed to connect the neighborhood to the bus stop on East Allen St. Mike asked for a review 
of the Lafountain-Dion Street scoping study recommendations. Jon and Ryan reviewed the 
recommendations for sidewalks on both streets, for parking removal along Lafountain Street, the 
narrowing of the vehicle travel lanes, the placement of street trees and amenity belts, and the 
movement of curbs. Ryan noted the need to possibly shift the location of the water main away 
from houses to prevent more adverse impacts. Jon, Ryan, and Ravi stated the staff time and 
resources needed for scoping studies to be successful, and the need for them to be a year-long 
process. Brian asked about sequencing short-term and long-term recommendations from 
scoping studies. Jon discussed coordinating improvements with other projects, and, if needed, 
having City staff repave the road and restripe it according to the recommendation.
Mike asked about the Dion Street and East Allen Street intersection, and the types of 
improvements that could be done. Jon said that the City and CCRPC will need to do traffic 
counts after the bridge construction is complete—after the traffic normalizes—to determine 
possible improvements. Ryan reviewed the slated changes to the East Allen Street and I-89 
intersection to address potential traffic increases as part of the bridge project.
Brian asked about design choices to indicate entry into the gateway areas into the City. Jon 
discussed the median islands on Main Street at the northernmost portion, and noted that further 
discussion is needed for Malletts Bay Avenue and East Allen Street. Brian asked about roadway 
signage. Jon said that wayfinding signage is under discussion in the upcoming budget.
Eli asked which streets will need utility improvements first, and how that will feed into the 
Planning Commission’s discussions. Jon said that the water distribution system is typically the 
main priority, and that the water distribution master plan is currently being updated which will 
inform which water mains will need to be replaced. Ravi said that the water distribution master 
plan was noted in the Planning Commission’s current work plan, and that he hopes the Planning 
Commission will have conversations to make sure the City’s infrastructure matches the 
regulations after the water distribution master plan is complete. Jon said that the water 
distribution master plan would provide more information on how much more development a 
water main along a specific street could serve. Mike asked if a street of single-family homes 
became duplexes, would the water line serving those buildings be sufficient. Jon said the water 
line might be enough, and that the issue lies with whether buildings will require sprinklers. Mike 
suggested that this issue could be something the state legislature addresses at some point.
Mike asked about Gail Street. Ryan said that the outcome is to add a sidewalk, potentially with 
grant support, and that there are cost considerations for adding new sidewalks.
Discussion: Review of Boards, Committees, and Commission Structure
This item was tabled until the next meeting.
City Updates
Updates from the Mayor
Thomas reviewed the presentation University of Vermont Center For Rural Studies 
gave to City Council on the Equitable Housing Needs Assessment, the opening of 
the new hotel, the discussions on electric vehicle charging stations at City Hall 
during the last City Council meeting.
Updates from the Inclusion and Belonging Commission
Updates from City Staff
Ravi said his main focus has been on the Comprehensive Plan, and that zoning 
has slowed down considerably.
Other Business
Adjourn
Motion by: Matt
Second: Ruby
Meeting End Time: 8:08 pm
I.
II.
III.
IV.
V.
VI.
VII.
A.
B.
C.
VIII.
IX.

asked why the sidewalk on East Spring Street will be placed on the south side. Ryan explained 
that the location of subsurface infrastructure, the potential impacts of turning movements at the 
intersection on pedestrian safety, and costs.
Mike asked about West Spring Street. Ravi said that the intent is to be determined, and that the 
City would need to consider how it is coordinating bicycle and pedestrian improvements on 
Malletts Bay and East Spring Street to ensure wider connectivity. Ryan added that the pavement 
condition of Spring Street is poor, and that resurfacing is likely to happen before any 
investigations into improving connectivity.
Ravi said that North Street is in need of a sidewalk north of Pine Street because the 
neighborhood is cut off from the rest of the City. Mike asked about the presence of sidewalks in 
the northern portion of North Street. Jon said that the side streets off North Street—Cedar 
Street, Dufresne Drive, and Brisson Court—have sidewalks but North Street does not. Matt 
underscored the challenges of walking students from the school to Landry Park safely, and the 
options are limited. Jon reviewed the citywide traffic calming review, stating that North Street 
qualified for traffic calming, which may lend to building out a sidewalk in the long term. Mike 
asked about the access between North Street and Tigan Street. Ryan said that the City owns 
the parcel on which a path exists, but no formal right-of-way from Tigan Street to the beginning 
of that path. Jon said hat he has encouraged community members to reach out to the 
businesses on Tigan Street to formalize the connection between Tigan Street and the path to 
North Street.
Ravi said that the City has completed a scoping study for Lafountain Street and Dion Street, and 
that the City will need to work on the next steps towards implementation. Jon said that Public 
Works looks to coordinate utility improvements with roadway improvements, that the water main 
on Lafountain Street has had many water breaks, and that replacing the water main is 
highlighted in the City’s water distribution master plan. Jon said that the sidewalk on Dion Street 
is needed to connect the neighborhood to the bus stop on East Allen St. Mike asked for a review 
of the Lafountain-Dion Street scoping study recommendations. Jon and Ryan reviewed the 
recommendations for sidewalks on both streets, for parking removal along Lafountain Street, the 
narrowing of the vehicle travel lanes, the placement of street trees and amenity belts, and the 
movement of curbs. Ryan noted the need to possibly shift the location of the water main away 
from houses to prevent more adverse impacts. Jon, Ryan, and Ravi stated the staff time and 
resources needed for scoping studies to be successful, and the need for them to be a year-long 
process. Brian asked about sequencing short-term and long-term recommendations from 
scoping studies. Jon discussed coordinating improvements with other projects, and, if needed, 
having City staff repave the road and restripe it according to the recommendation.
Mike asked about the Dion Street and East Allen Street intersection, and the types of 
improvements that could be done. Jon said that the City and CCRPC will need to do traffic 
counts after the bridge construction is complete—after the traffic normalizes—to determine 
possible improvements. Ryan reviewed the slated changes to the East Allen Street and I-89 
intersection to address potential traffic increases as part of the bridge project.
Brian asked about design choices to indicate entry into the gateway areas into the City. Jon 
discussed the median islands on Main Street at the northernmost portion, and noted that further 
discussion is needed for Malletts Bay Avenue and East Allen Street. Brian asked about roadway 
signage. Jon said that wayfinding signage is under discussion in the upcoming budget.
Eli asked which streets will need utility improvements first, and how that will feed into the 
Planning Commission’s discussions. Jon said that the water distribution system is typically the 
main priority, and that the water distribution master plan is currently being updated which will 
inform which water mains will need to be replaced. Ravi said that the water distribution master 
plan was noted in the Planning Commission’s current work plan, and that he hopes the Planning 
Commission will have conversations to make sure the City’s infrastructure matches the 
regulations after the water distribution master plan is complete. Jon said that the water 
distribution master plan would provide more information on how much more development a 
water main along a specific street could serve. Mike asked if a street of single-family homes 
became duplexes, would the water line serving those buildings be sufficient. Jon said the water 
line might be enough, and that the issue lies with whether buildings will require sprinklers. Mike 
suggested that this issue could be something the state legislature addresses at some point.
Mike asked about Gail Street. Ryan said that the outcome is to add a sidewalk, potentially with 
grant support, and that there are cost considerations for adding new sidewalks.
Discussion: Review of Boards, Committees, and Commission Structure
This item was tabled until the next meeting.
